core_dimensions.label: Discreetness
core_dimensions.description: How closely the product functions and presents as ordinary eyewear in routine public use, including visual bulk, obvious electronics, capture indicators, and everyday social practicality.

core_dimensions.label: Camera
core_dimensions.description: The usefulness of the outward-facing camera system for wearer-perspective capture, including still/video capability, access, limitations, and practical image capture rather than camera presence alone.

core_dimensions.label: Visual AI
core_dimensions.description: Can the glasses understand what the wearer is looking at and turn visual context into useful machine understanding, including object/text/environment recognition where supported?

core_dimensions.label: Hackability
core_dimensions.description: The practical experimentation surface: BLE or wired access, SDK/API access, firmware paths, reverse-engineering potential, sideloading, exposed interfaces, and community tooling.

core_dimensions.label: Owner Control
core_dimensions.description: How much meaningful control remains with the owner, including direct device access, replaceable AI, local processing, custom endpoints, sideloading, and freedom from a single prescribed vendor path.

core_dimensions.label: Android Compatibility
core_dimensions.description: The depth and quality of Android support, from basic companion-app compatibility through direct SDK/device access, standard interfaces, and owner-controlled integration.

migration.rule: Do not relabel a broader legacy score as a Core score unless the meaning is equivalent. Unknown remains unknown until evidence supports a judgment.
